samples.summary: The tooltip's offline-offer sentence is never exercised: `tooltipFor` is only ever called with `offerOffline: false`
samples.evidence:
`tooltipFor(state, pendingSince, connected, offerOffline, lapse)` is called in exactly two places in the suite — `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:919` (`tooltipFor('not-saved', null, false, false, lapse)`) and `:966` (`tooltipFor('saved', null, true, false, 'another-tab')`). Both pass `offerOffline: false`, so the branch at `sync-status-tooltip.ts:108-110` producing `' Click to save documents you open later on this device. These changes stay in this tab.'` is never evaluated by any assertion.

The wiring tests cannot reach it either: `strandedUnderScopes` (chip test ~line 990) never stubs `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and `offerOffline` is false; and the `describe('the offer to turn offline saving on')` block, which *does* stub the version and gets `offerOffline === true`, only clicks the chip/toast and asserts the toast `action.label` — it never focuses the chip to read the tooltip.

The one test that guards this exact wording property — `'never promises to save the changes it is shown beside'` — asserts `options.action.label` (the toast button), not the tooltip sentence. The source comment at `sync-status-tooltip.ts:101-107` states the harm being guarded: "Somebody who read the older wording could reasonably click, then reload, and lose exactly the work the sentence promised to keep." That regression would ship with a fully green suite.

samples.summary: The new connected/disconnected split in the `not-saved` tooltip is only tested on the disconnected arm
samples.evidence: `tooltipFor` gained a `connected` parameter in this diff, driving `why = connected ? '…were rejected by the server…' : '…because the connection dropped.'` (`sync-status-tooltip.ts:89-91`). Every `not-saved` assertion goes through the helper at `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:919`, `const stranded = (lapse) => tooltipFor('not-saved', null, false, false, lapse)` — hard-coded `connected: false`. samples.summary: `DurableYorkieProvider`'s lapse mapping is untested for every reason except `dropped` — `out-of-space`, `write-failed`, `too-large` and `unreportable` are never asserted as published values
samples.evidence:
`durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:213-227` computes `lapse` from `lost | persistDisabled | outOfSpace | writesFailing | unreportable`, including the `QuotaExceededError` → `setOutOfSpace(true)` detection at :169-176. `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` renders only a `Probe` over `useDocumentDurability()` — it never mounts a `useDurabilityLapse()` probe, so it asserts durability drops but never which reason is published. `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`'s `describe('the lapse it publishes')` covers `not-enabled`, `not-permitted`, `another-tab`, `none` and `dropped` — none of the four store-side reasons.

Consequently `LAPSE_REASONS.unreportable` (`sync-status-tooltip.ts:43-44`) is dead to the suite in both directions: no test passes that lapse to `tooltipFor`, and no test proves a provider ever emits it. The design requirement quoted in the code ("Its tooltip must name which case applies") is therefore unverified for the causes only the durable client can observe — e.g. a quota failure surfacing as "This device could not be written to." instead of "This device is out of local storage space." would ship undetected.

samples.summary: `dropAllForUser`'s `keepArchives` option has no caller and no test, so its documented behaviour is unverified
samples.evidence: `grep keepArchives` across `packages/frontend` returns only three declaration/usage sites in the implementation (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1135, 1166, 1173`) and the pass-through in `offline-erase.ts:30`. No caller ever supplies it — `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` calls `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` with no options — and no test in `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts`, `-cleanup.test.ts` or `offline-erase.test.ts` passes it. samples.summary: The new `runSpellRecheck` swallow and the stale-session repaint guard in the docs editor have no test
samples.evidence: The diff splits `runSpellRecheck` into a swallowing wrapper plus `recheckSpelling`, and adds `if (spellSession !== session || !spellEnabled) return;` before `renderPaintOnly()` (editor.ts ~:3237). `grep 'runSpellRecheck|recheckSpelling|recheckBlocks'` in `packages/docs` matches only `src/view/editor.ts`, `src/spell/session.ts` and `test/spell/session.test.ts` — the last tests `SpellSession.recheckBlocks` directly, not the editor wrapper. `packages/docs/test/view/` holds ~60 `editor-*.test.ts` files, so the editor is testable in this suite, but none covers spell recheck: neither the swallow (a rejected lazy dictionary import must not escape) nor the guard (no repaint after `destroy()` or a session swap) is asserted.

samples.summary: `hasOfflinePersistenceConsent` has no direct test, and the branch it exists for — pending identity on a device with no consent rendering instantly — is uncovered
samples.evidence:
`grep hasOfflinePersistenceConsent` across `packages/frontend` returns only the declaration (`offline-persistence-preference.ts:123`) and one consumer (`collab-document-provider.tsx:241`). `offline-persistence-preference.test.ts` never imports or calls it.

Indirectly, `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`'s `'waits for the identity rather than reading a pending one as "not eligible"'` covers only the `true` arm (it sets `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled('7', true)` before making the identity pending). If the function wrongly answered `true`, every editor on a fresh device would render a null frame while the identity query resolves, and nothing would fail.

samples.summary: The chip's `!!userId` guard on the offline offer is never exercised — every chip test seeds an identity
samples.evidence: `offerOffline` (`sync-status-chip.tsx:115-120`) requires `!!userId`, and the comment justifies it as the anonymous share-link case ("never without an account to attribute the choice to"). But the `render()` helper added to `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` unconditionally does `client.setQueryData(['me','optional'], { id: 7, ... })`, and `sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx` does the same. No test renders the chip with `me` absent, so the one deployment where the chip is mounted without an account — the public `/shared/:token` route — has no coverage for either the button rendering or `turnOnOfflineSaving`'s `if (!userId) return` early exit.

samples.evidence: The `saved-locally` branch added at `sync-status-chip.tsx:235-252` sets `warned.current = true` specifically so the recovery arm at :286-301 retracts it and confirms once the work reaches the server. In `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx`, `success` and `dismiss` mocks are declared and cleared (lines 21/23, 202-203) but the only assertions on `success` are at :548 and :580, both inside `describe('the offer to turn offline saving on')` where the success toast comes from `turnOnOfflineSaving`, not from the recovery arm. `dismiss` is never asserted at all (grep for `dismiss.` yields only `dismiss.mockClear()`). samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser`'s skip branch in orphan collection is untested
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters out keys where `belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)` matches `wb:{secret}:{otherUserId}:`. The only orphan test is `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts:127` (`'is collected rather than living forever out of reach'`), which uses the bare key `"doc-a"` — the regex matches nothing, so only the `false` path runs. No test seeds an orphan under a `wb:…:{other-user}:…` key to prove another account's orphan is spared. A regex regression here would either sweep another account's row or, in the other direction, permanently strand an orphan holding document content that `dropAllForUser` cannot reach.

samples.summary: Nothing verifies the `OfflineRuntime` effect does not re-run on in-app navigation, which is the whole reason `navigateRef` exists
samples.evidence: `navigateRef` (`offline-runtime.tsx:54-58`) is introduced specifically so `useNavigate`'s unstable identity cannot re-trigger the effect — the comment lists the cost: "a new database handle, the thirty-day sweep again, the archive listing again, and a title fetch per archive" on every navigation. `offline-runtime.test.tsx` mocks `react-router-dom` with `useNavigate: () => navigate` returning one stable mock, so the instability being guarded cannot occur in the test, and no case re-renders with a changed navigate to assert `collectStale`/`fetchDocuments` were called exactly once. Removing `navigateRef` and adding `navigate` to the deps array would leave the suite green.

samples.summary: The path-traversal test was weakened from "every request URL encodes the id" to "some request URL does"
samples.evidence: The per-URL assertion `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` inside the loop was replaced by a single `paths.some(...)` check at :170-174, while the loop now only keeps the negative `not.toContain('/auth/logout')`. The justification (a companion `fetchDocuments()` request carries no id) is sound and the negative check still runs over every URL, so the core traversal property survives — but the weakened form no longer requires each *id-bearing* request in a multi-request call (`deleteWorkspace`, `removeMember`, both of which now issue `fetchWorkspace` + `fetchDocuments` before the DELETE) to encode it. A narrower predicate — asserting it of every path that is not the id-less listing — would keep the original strength.

verdict.reason: The offer sentence at sync-status-tooltip.ts:108-110 is evaluated by no assertion anywhere in the repo. `tooltipFor` has exactly two consumers (sync-status-chip.tsx:383 and sync-status-chip.test.tsx), and both test call sites (:919, :966) pass offerOffline:false. The only tests that open the Radix tooltip to read rendered text (:1007-1009, :1042-1044) never stub `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and `offerOffline` is false; their assertions are about lapse reasons and 'exist only in this tab', and :1048-1051 explicitly declines to assert on 'this device'. The test that guards this exact wording property, 'never promises to save the changes it is shown beside' (:638-664), asserts the toast `action.label` (sync-status-chip.tsx:277), not the tooltip string. Repo-wide greps for the sentence and its fragments ('Click to save documents you open later', 'stay in this tab', 'open later', 'offerOffline', /later/i across all test files) return only source hits; no e2e suite exists. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: the branch carries an explicitly documented anti-data-loss wording guard (comment at :101-107 — click, reload, lose the work the sentence promised to keep), and a regression to a promise-bearing phrasing would ship with a fully green suite.
